source_text: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) have reviewed this body of evidence, concluding that preventive benefits—encompassing reduced HIV/STI acquisition, UTIs, penile cancer, and balanitis—outweigh procedural risks when performed neonatally or under medical conditions.
